_comment: Tool calls put to `gnomon guard` AND to gnomon's own turn loop, under the same surface,
and the decision each must reach. One file, read by both sides:
packages/gnomon-core/src/guard.test.ts runs every case through runAgenticTurn (a scripted
model makes the call; an approval request means `ask`, a refusal code 2-4 means `deny`,
anything else `allow`) and through guardToolCall, and asserts the two agree with each other
and with `expect`. packages/gnomon-cli/src/guard.test.ts puts the same cases to the real
`gnomon guard` binary. A rule that moved in one place and not the other fails here.
`expect` is keyed by the [approval] gate the surface declares. A gate missing from a case
is not run under it (an allowed call under `never` really runs in the loop, and some are
not worth running: a fetch to a name that will not resolve).
The surface: `surface` below, written into a fresh git repository and committed, with
src/a.ts holding `old\n`.

surface.roles.toml:
[roles.implement]
model = "m"
tools = ["read", "write", "edit", "bash", "webfetch"]
write_allow = ["src/**", "tests/**"]
bash_deny = ['\bgit\s+push\b[^|;&]*\s(--force|-f)\b', '\brm\s+-rf\s+/']

[roles.readonly]
model = "m"
tools = ["read", "bash"]
bash_allow = ['^ls\b', '^cat\b', '^git\s+(status|diff|log)\b']
surface.tools.toml:
[[tools]]
name = "read"
enabled = true

[[tools]]
name = "write"
enabled = true

[[tools]]
name = "edit"
enabled = true

[[tools]]
name = "bash"
enabled = true

[[tools]]
name = "webfetch"
enabled = true
surface.policy.toml:
[approval]
gate = "{{gate}}"
repo_code = true

[sandbox]
level = "confined"
network = true

cases.name: python code writing through a name bound to a path outside write_allow is denied (G1c T3 r1, verbatim)

input.command:
python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path

changelog = Path("CHANGELOG.md")
text = changelog.read_text()
old = "# Changelog\n\n## 0.4.0"
new = "# Changelog\n\n## Unreleased\n- Add `Stock.restock(sku, qty)`, which adds a positive quantity and returns the new level.\n\n## 0.4.0"
assert text.count(old) == 1, "unexpected CHANGELOG layout"
changelog.write_text(text.replace(old, new))

pyproject = Path("pyproject.toml")
text = pyproject.read_text()
old = 'version = "0.4.0"'
new = 'version = "0.5.0"'
assert text.count(old) == 1, "unexpected pyproject layout"
pyproject.write_text(text.replace(old, new))
print("updated CHANGELOG.md and pyproject.toml")
PY

a shell write inside write_allow is the gate's call

_comment: Governance levels (CONTRACTS.md §36): the same calls at each of observe, advise, prevent and
enforce, put to BOTH gnomon's own loop and `gnomon guard` (packages/gnomon-core/src/guard.test.ts,
and the real binary in packages/gnomon-cli/src/guard.test.ts). The surface is `surface` above with
policy.toml replaced by `policy` below, `{{level}}` set to the level under test.
`verdict` is what the rules say and `rule` / `family` name the first rule that says it (for an ask:
the rule that asks). `expect` is the decision per level, derived by one rule: below prevent a deny
or ask in a levelled family is allow (recorded, not applied); `rules` has a floor of prevent;
structural rules (`family` null) are never levelled. enforce decides as prevent in this build.
`decided_by` names the rule the decision reports at a level where it is not `rule`: a verdict
levelled away lets the next rule on the same call decide.
Every case is safe to RUN, because observe and advise run it: no command here reaches the
network or leaves the scratch repository. `ci` has no rule yet (shared-governance PR 3) and
`secrets` only the read sandbox, so neither has more cases.
levels.policy:
[approval]
gate = "on_write"
repo_code = true

[sandbox]
level = "confined"
network = false

[governance]
level = "{{level}}"

cases.name: bash_deny: a force-push
bash_allow: a segment off the list
approval: an ordinary command under on_write
repo_code: make runs the Makefile
write_allow: a write outside it
write_allow: a shell append outside it
approval: a write inside write_allow under on_write
sandbox: a read outside the repository
network: webfetch under network = false (and a file: URL, which never fetches)
network: a named client under network = false
surface: a write to .gnomon/ (rules floor: prevent)
surface: a shell append to .gnomon/ (rules floor: prevent)
git_hooks: git config core.hooksPath (rules floor: prevent)
record: a write into the audit trail (rules floor: prevent)
a levelled bash_deny does not hide a surface write on the same line

cases.name: tools: a role without write (structural, never levelled)
malformed: a non-string command (structural, never levelled)
a read inside the repository: nothing to level
